subject: Marketplace branding & SLA governance — ACME Analytics listing
messages:
From: Devon Green <devon.green@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace Reviewer <aws-marketplace-reviewer@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing copy + SLA question

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on — we want to finalize our AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace listing this week. Attached is our proposed listing copy and logo pack (Listing_Copy_v1.docx, Marketplace_Graphics_v3.zip). Two quick compliance questions from the marketplace checklist:

- Can Redwood support the “24/7 enterprise support” claim on the listing if our support contract is business-hours + paid 24x7 upgrades?
- Marketplace team flagged use of the phrase “enterprise-grade” and asked for evidence. What level of proof do you typically provide?

We’re targeting co-sell enablement next quarter and need the listing live by Aug 1. Any guidance appreciated.

Thanks,
Devon Green
Head of Partnerships, Acme Analytics
devon.green@acmeanalytics.com

P.S. CC’ing the AWS reviewer so we can close any policy gaps quickly.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Devon Green <devon.green@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing copy + SLA question

Thanks Devon — got it. I reviewed the attachments briefly. Quick response and proposed plan:

1) Support claim: Marketplace requires the listing to reflect the publicly-offered support entitlement. If Acme’s standard offering is business-hours with a paid 24x7 add-on, we should not state “24/7 enterprise support” as a default. Two options:
   - Change copy to: “Business-hours support with optional 24x7 incident coverage”
   - Or, add a clear footnote on the listing and link to the support page that describes the paid 24x7 upgrade.
2) “Enterprise-grade” language: Marketplace reviewers often want measurable signals. We can provide:
   - SOC2 Type II attestation (if available)
   - Customer logos/case studies and uptime/SLI numbers
   - A short bullet list of tech capabilities (dedicated deployments, private VPC options) to qualify the claim

I’m looping in Vanessa and Laura to do a policy + marketing pass and produce suggested alternate phrasing and an SLA table that maps to marketplace expectations. Vanessa — can you take a look at the logo/spec guidance, and Laura can you draft conservative copy alternatives?

Next steps: internal align -> send a single consolidated file to AWS reviewer for a pre-check. If acceptable, schedule a 20-min call with Acme and AWS reviewer on Thu.

– Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing copy + SLA question

Quick policy notes from the marketplace side — pulled from recent AWS/Azure reviewer guidance: 

- Branding & logos: marketplace requires a transparent PNG at 1024x1024 and an alternate square with safe margin. Avoid altering partner program badges. Include a short manifest of assets and usage rights.
- Claims: terms like “enterprise-grade”, “best-in-class”, or “bank-grade” trigger reviewer requests for substantiation. Acceptable evidence: SOC2 report, uptime SLA (e.g., 99.9% monthly), customer success references (business POC).
- Support SLA on the listing: must not advertise paid-only entitlements as included. If you offer paid 24x7, list the baseline and the upgrade path clearly. For co-sell eligibility, AWS sometimes requires a named escalation contact (email + phone) and a 24/7 incident process documented in the listing or linked docs.

I recommend the conservative copy option Karthik suggested. I’ll annotate the Listing_Copy_v1.docx with: 1) alternate phrasing, 2) logo manifest checklist, and 3) a short “evidence” appendix we can send to the reviewer.

Vanessa Ortiz
Partner Programs Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing copy + SLA question

Adding suggested marketing-friendly but compliant alternatives and an SLA mapping table (see attached Acme_Support_SLA_Table.xlsx):

- Replace “enterprise-grade” with “production-ready and designed for scale” — more descriptive and less subjective.
- For the support line: 
  - Listing: “Business-hours support; optional 24x7 incident coverage available”
  - In the SLA table (attached) define P1/P2/P3 response times for each support tier and indicate what’s included in the base vs paid tiers. Example: P1 (critical) — base: 4-hour response (business hrs); paid 24x7: 1-hour response and dedicated escalation route.

Jonas — please confirm there are no platform-level restrictions from a technical enablement perspective (e.g., dedicated escalation contact).

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Marketing Manager, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Finalized listing language & next steps

Hi Devon (and AWS reviewer),

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal review we propose the following final listing language to address the marketplace guidance:

- Support line (listing): “Business-hours support; optional 24x7 incident coverage available. See support page for upgrade details.”
- Capability line: “Production-ready inference platform with private deployment and dedicated capacity options.”

Attachments included for your review: Listing_Copy_v1.docx (annotated), Marketplace_Graphics_v3.zip, Acme_Support_SLA_Table.xlsx (breaks out base vs paid response times). We are explicitly NOT using the phrase “enterprise-grade” on the public listing; instead we’ll include supporting evidence (SOC2 doc / uptime metrics) in the reviewer package.

Action items:
- Devon: confirm Acme is comfortable with the support wording and the plan to link to the support page for paid 24x7 add-on.
- AWS reviewer: can you do a quick pre-check and confirm if the revised language + attachments are sufficient for co-sell enablement? If you prefer, we can hop on a 20-min sync Thu 7/24 to walk through the assets.

Thanks — looping Jonas for the escalation contact that AWS may require.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
